questions.answer:

Apply the model for Far-Field Fraunhofer Diffraction and Rayleigh Distance under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Replacing \(a\) by \(2a\) gives \[d_R'=\frac{(2a)^2}{\lambda}=4d_R.\] The larger aperture has four times the maximum quadratic path phase at the same distance. Final result: doubling the aperture width increases the Rayleigh distance, and hence the far-field distance scale, by a factor of four.
